findings.issue_text: **1. `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11` — migration crashes on nearly every existing site.**
**2. `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` — migrated rows bypass normalization, silently breaking embedding after upgrade.**

The raw setting value is inserted verbatim, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17`) matches against `URI(...).host` — i.e. a bare hostname. The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly tolerated `http://`-prefixed entries (`h.sub(/^https?\:\/\//, '')`), so real sites have values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` stored. Those migrate to rows that can never match, and embedding breaks with a 403 on the first request after upgrade — with no error surfaced to the admin. Note the new spec at `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:68-69` fabricates exactly these shapes and only passes because the model callback normalizes them; the migration has no such callback.
**3. `app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3` — `embed: :ids` without root sideloading; the admin page renders nothing usable.**
**4. `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8` — `nil.sub!` raises on missing host, returning 500 instead of 422.**

`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` straight through (`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23`). Submitting the form with an empty host (or any client/API caller omitting the key) hits `self.host.sub!` on `nil` and raises `NoMethodError` before validation ever runs. The client-side `cantSave` guard masks this in the happy path, but it is trivially reachable via the API and via a whitespace-only host. There is also no `validates_presence_of :host`.
**7. `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17` — case-insensitive lookup only lowercases one side.**
**9. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-42` — category is now passed as an integer id where a name was previously passed; unverified and untested.**

`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each assert only `Controller < Admin::AdminController` — a tautology that exercises no behavior. There are no specs for: `EmbeddableHost` validation/normalization (the `before_validation` scheme/path stripping, the format regex), `record_for_host` / `host_allowed?` (including the nil-referer and bare-hostname cases), CRUD through the admin controller, the uncategorized fallback at `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25`, or the migration backfill. Issues 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 above are all things a modest spec would have caught.
**12. `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24-25` — category integrity is enforced only by the DB.**

**13. `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11` — `update` is a no-op.** It ignores the request body and re-renders the unchanged `@embedding`. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6:6`) calls `embedding.update({})`, and `embedding.hbs` has no save button wired to it — so both the route (`config/routes.rb:139`) and the action are dead code today. Either remove them or implement the intended embedding-level settings.

**14. `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:3` and `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3` — redundant filters.** `Admin::AdminController` already applies `ensure_logged_in`/`ensure_staff`, and every route is additionally behind `AdminConstraint`. Harmless but noise; drop them.

**15. `app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14` — three method overrides that just re-return the attribute.** `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` already does exactly this. Delete the bodies (and the trailing blank line at :16).

**20. `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2` — the format regex still permits a path** (`(\/.*)?`) even though the `before_validation` hook strips paths before validation runs, and the `{2,5}` TLD bound rejects legitimate modern TLDs (`.online`, `.software`). Tighten the regex to match what is actually storable.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **1. `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-11` — migration crashes on nearly every existing site.**

adjudication.rationale: The migration unconditionally does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when looking up the `embed_category` site setting via a join (and later does similar `[0]['value']` lookups). On most sites `site_settings` only contains overridden settings, so there may be no row for `embed_category` (or it may not match a category name), making `execute(...)[0]` nil and causing a crash (`NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`) during migration. This is a concrete, verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` can set `host.host` to `nil` if the `:host` key is missing (or `params[:embeddable_host]` itself is nil, which would error even earlier). In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)`, which will raise `NoMethodError` when `self.host` is `nil`, preventing validations from running. There is also no `validates_presence_of :host`, and the existing `validates_format_of` doesn’t prevent the callback crash.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the migration builds raw SQL with direct Ruby interpolation of `h` from `site_settings` into `execute "... VALUES ('#{h}', ... )"`. Even though it’s wrapped in single quotes, it is not escaped/quoted via the connection adapter, so a value containing `'` (or other SQL metacharacters) can break the migration and could allow SQL injection in principle. This is verifiable in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` inside `records.each`.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` and does not add any index on `host`. Both points are directly verifiable in the diff. `force: true` will drop an existing table if present (risking data loss in non-pristine environments), and the codebase adds lookups by host (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), so having no index on `host` is a concrete schema/performance defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **9. `app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-42` — category is now passed as an integer id where a name was previously passed; unverified and untested.**

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the code changes `category: SiteSetting.embed_category` to `category: eh.try(:category_id)`. The finding claims this is “unverified and untested”, but the diff adds explicit test coverage in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserting the created topic’s category equals `embeddable_host.category`, which exercises this path. Also, nothing in the diff shows that passing an integer `category_id` to `PostCreator` is incorrect (it is commonly accepted). Therefore the finding’s stated problem is not verifiably present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each assert only `Controller < Admin::AdminController` — a tautology that exercises no behavior. There are no specs for: `EmbeddableHost` validation/normalization (the `before_validation` scheme/path stripping, the format regex), `record_for_host` / `host_allowed?` (including the nil-referer and bare-hostname cases), CRUD through the admin controller, the uncategorized fallback at `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25`, or the migration backfill. Issues 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 above are all things a modest spec would have caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add two near-tautological controller specs that only assert inheritance, but the finding’s broader claim that there are *no* specs for EmbeddableHost normalization/validation and `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?` is contradicted by the diff: `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` explicitly tests scheme/path stripping and `host_allowed?` with multiple hosts, and `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` covers the “no referer” rejection path. The remaining items (CRUD via admin controller, uncategorized fallback, migration backfill) are indeed not covered, but “missing tests” is not a verifiable correctness/security defect in the code itself, and the finding is materially overstated/misreads what was added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **12. `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24-25` — category integrity is enforced only by the DB.**

adjudication.rationale: In `save_host`, the controller blindly assigns `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (falling back to uncategorized if blank) and there is no model-level validation that the referenced category exists. However, the finding’s claim that “category integrity is enforced only by the DB” is not verifiable from the diff: the migration only adds `null: false` on `category_id` and does not add a foreign key, so the DB is not shown enforcing referential integrity either. As written, the finding misstates what’s enforced and where.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **13. `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11` — `update` is a no-op.** It ignores the request body and re-renders the unchanged `@embedding`. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6:6`) calls `embedding.update({})`, and `embedding.hbs` has no save button wired to it — so both the route (`config/routes.rb:139`) and the action are dead code today. Either remove them or implement the intended embedding-level settings.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, the method ignores any incoming params/body and simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, so a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` cannot change anything (it is effectively a no-op). On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (sending an empty update), but `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` contains only per-host CRUD UI (`embeddable-host` component save/delete and an `addHost` button) and does not wire any button/action to `saveChanges`. Thus, the PUT route/action are presently unused and, even if invoked, would not persist changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **14. `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:3` and `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3` — redundant filters.** `Admin::AdminController` already applies `ensure_logged_in`/`ensure_staff`, and every route is additionally behind `AdminConstraint`. Harmless but noise; drop them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both new controllers explicitly adding `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` (and `:fetch_embedding` for `EmbeddingController`). Whether this is redundant depends on what `Admin::AdminController` already does, which is not shown in the diff, so the claim can’t be verified from the provided changes. Even if redundant, it’s harmless and not a clear bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff—at most a maintainability/style preference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **15. `app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14` — three method overrides that just re-return the attribute.** `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` already does exactly this. Delete the bodies (and the trailing blank line at :16).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHostSerializer`, the `id`, `host`, and `category_id` methods simply return `object.id/host/category_id`, which is redundant given `attributes :id, :host, :category_id`. However, this is not a bug or correctness/security defect introduced by the diff—it's a minor refactor/style cleanup suggestion. The serializer will work the same either way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **20. `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2` — the format regex still permits a path** (`(\/.*)?`) even though the `before_validation` hook strips paths before validation runs, and the `{2,5}` TLD bound rejects legitimate modern TLDs (`.online`, `.software`). Tighten the regex to match what is actually storable.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model introduces `validates_format_of :host` with a hard TLD length cap `\.[a-z]{2,5}`, which will reject many legitimate modern domains (e.g. `.online`, `.museum`, etc.) and therefore prevents saving valid embeddable hosts. The regex also allows an optional path `(\/.*)?` even though the `before_validation` callback strips paths (`sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`) before validation runs, making that part of the regex inconsistent with what is actually stored (though mostly redundant rather than harmful).
